title: Three-Dimensional Spheroid Culture Reveals Differential Ferroptosis Susceptibility in Human Ovarian Cancer Cells
content: Ferroptosis, an iron-dependent form of regulated cell death driven by lipid peroxidation, represents a promising therapeutic vulnerability in recalcitrant tumors. However, standard two-dimensional (2D) monolayer models fail to reproduce the physiological architecture and metabolic constraints governing redox homeostasis in solid tumors. Here, we evaluated erastin-induced ferroptosis in OVCAR-8 (OV-8) and PA1 ovarian cancer cells cultured as 2D monolayers and three-dimensional (3D) spheroids. In 2D culture, erastin induced comparable concentration-dependent cytotoxicity in both lines, which was attenuated by deferoxamine and ferrostatin-1 (FES), and accompanied by glutathione depletion, malondialdehyde (MDA) accumulation, and upregulation of CHAC1 and HMOX1. Strikingly, 3D culture revealed a profound phenotypic divergence: OV-8 spheroids remained sensitive—displaying disrupted architecture, elevated MDA, and loss of cell viability that was rescued by ferrostatin-1—whereas PA1 spheroids acquired significant resistance to erastin. NMR-based metabolomic profiling of 2D cultures revealed that erastin induced concurrent depletion of intracellular glucose and lactate in PA1 cells, reflecting diminished glycolytic dependence and potential redirection toward NADPH-generating pathways. Concomitant glutamine depletion and glutamate accumulation suggest enhanced glutaminolysis for NADPH generation and antioxidant support. Conversely, OV-8 cells accumulated structural and alternative amino acids. These findings demonstrate that 3D tumor architecture reveals cell-line-specific redox and metabolic adaptations obscured in 2D culture, underscoring the importance of physiologically relevant models for evaluating ferroptosis-targeted therapeutics.
